Entry/Spare Poly

Dragon Cotton Candy Poly

A fun, honest spare ball. Dead-straight where you aim it, in a cotton candy swirl.

The Dragon Cotton Candy is a durable polyester spare ball, ideal for beginners learning the game, kids, and experienced bowlers alike.

Use it as a dedicated spare ball to pick off single pins like the 10-pin, flush and repeatable every time.

Who It Is Built For

Match It To Your Game

Spare Shooting

Polyester does not react to oil, so the Cotton Candy holds a dead-straight line across any pattern, the tool for flushing corner pins like the 10-pin with confidence.

Beginners & Youth

A durable, forgiving first ball for learning a straight, repeatable shot, with a bright cotton candy look kids love.

A Dedicated Spare Ball

Experienced bowlers keep one in the bag to shoot spares flush without chasing hook, a simple, reliable second ball at a value price.

The Engine

3 Piece Core

The 3 Piece Core is a symmetric pancake core, the simplest and most predictable shape in bowling. At 15 lb it measures 2.69 RG and a .006 differential, numbers built for a straight, true roll instead of hook.

That very low differential means almost no track flare, so the ball goes where you aim it, exactly what a spare ball should be: repeatable and honest, shot after shot.

The Coverstock

Polyester

The cover is durable polyester, the classic non-reactive spare-ball shell. It does not respond to oil, so it holds a straight line across any pattern for flush, repeatable spare shots.

The blue, pink, and white cotton candy swirl keeps it fun and eye-catching, a spare ball with personality that is built to last. USBC approved.

Ball Care

Keep It Lethal

  • Wipe the cover with a microfiber towel to keep the finish clean.
  • Polyester is low maintenance and does not need resurfacing to keep its straight, predictable roll.
  • The Dragon Cotton Candy is sold undrilled. Have it drilled by a certified pro shop and fit it to your hand.

How to measure

These are measurements of the jersey laid flat, not of your body. The most reliable way to pick a size is to measure a shirt you already like wearing and match it to the table.

  1. Width. Lay the shirt flat and measure straight across from one underarm seam to the other.
  2. Length. Measure from the highest point of the shoulder, next to the collar, straight down to the hem.

A variance of up to 0.75 inches from the chart is normal on a printed-to-order garment.
